subject: Renewal proposal: hybrid retainer + elastic surge allowance
messages:
From: Nina Shah <nina.shah@elmhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: ElmHealth Procurement <procurement@elmhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window — exploring alternatives for next year

Hi Sofia,

We're approaching our renewal window with Redwood (contract ends 2025-09-30) and Procurement asked me to surface a couple of options for next year. Usage has clustered — baseline generation volume is steady, but we see frequent short bursts during weekly model training runs and product demos.

We'd like to explore a structure that reduces per-token variability for budgeting while still allowing for 2–3 monthly bursts of ~3x baseline without heavy overage penalties. Specifically: can Redwood propose a hybrid retainer + surge allowance (either pooled credits or an elastic burst buffer) and share estimated unit economics?

Also curious whether you can co-term our new add-on seats to the main renewal date vs. starting a separate 12-month clock for the add-on. Legal will want a simple SOW and an estimate they can put in the budget next week.

Can you send a short proposal and a sample SOW? If pricing needs an exec sign-off we can loop in procurement leadership.

Thanks — Nina
Nina Shah
Head of Procurement, ElmHealth
procurement@elmhealth.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window — exploring alternatives for next year

Hi Nina — thanks for the clear ask.

Short answer: yes. We have two practical constructs that fit your description and legal/budget preferences:

1) Hybrid retainer + burst pool
   - Monthly reserved baseline (committed units) priced at a discount vs on-demand.
   - A shared monthly burst pool of credits that covers spikes (credits priced at a mid-level rate — cheaper than on-demand but higher than committed unit).
   - Unused burst credits roll forward for up to 3 months.

2) Elastic surge lane (on-demand buffer with a capped surcharge)
   - Larger committed baseline, with an automatically enabled burst lane that caps surcharge at a fixed percentage above committed rate.
   - No credits to track; billing shows a separate line item for surge usage.

Both options can be structured to co-term add-ons by aligning the add-on commitment to the main renewal date and prorating the first partial period. We can include either approach in the SOW.

I'm attaching a short proposal and a draft SOW to make budget conversations straightforward. Ben and Marissa are looped for pricing options and legal/ops details.

If you prefer, we can do a 20-min call to walk through the two options tomorrow.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Director — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ElmHealth_Renewal_Proposal_v2.pdf, SOW_ElmHealth_Midterm.xlsx

Subject: FW: Renewal window — pricing sketch and internal ask

Sofia / Marissa — forwarding Nina's note. Quick internal sketch below (for the call):

- Current ElmHealth baseline: ~18M tokens / month (steady). Peak bursts: up to ~55M for 1–2 days.
- Option A (Hybrid retainer + burst pool)
   * Commit: 20M tokens/mo at 15% discount vs on-demand
   * Burst pool: 30M credits/month priced at 8% premium to committed per-token (i.e., cheaper than on-demand but higher than commit)
   * Roll-forward: up to 3 months on unused burst credits
   * Estimated blended unit price: ~X (we'll calculate exact blended $/1k tokens)
- Option B (Elastic surge lane)
   * Commit: 24M tokens/mo at 12% discount
   * Surge cap: surcharge at max +25% per token above committed rate; automatic fallback to cheaper compatible model if sustained for >6 hours
   * No credit accounting; cleaner invoicing.

Questions for Sofia: which packaging does ElmHealth prefer for budgeting simplicity?
Questions for Marissa: legal ops on SOW timing — can we create an addendum so add-on seats co-term without a separate 12-mo clock? If yes, we'll draft language to prorate first billing period and note renewal sync.

I'll run numbers for blended $/1k tokens and include a small exec concession bucket (one-time onboarding credit up to $5k) if they convert to a 12-month co-term.

— Ben

Subject: Renewal proposal attached — hybrid retainer + surge pool (recommended)

Hi Nina — following up with the attached proposal and draft SOW. TL;DR recommendation: Hybrid retainer + burst pool (Option A) because it preserves clear committed baseline pricing for budgeting while giving you predictable, managed headroom for short spikes. Key points: 

- Commit: 20M tokens/mo at 15% off on-demand.
- Burst pool: 30M credits/mo, priced at 8% above the committed unit rate. Unused burst credits roll forward for up to 3 months.
- Co-term: Add-on seats and new connectors can be co-termed to run to 2026-09-30; first partial billing period prorated to the renewal date.
- Exec concession: $5k onboarding credit if a 12-month co-term is signed by 2025-08-05.
- Billing: single invoice; burst usage line item separate for transparency.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Nina: confirm preferred option and whether Procurement needs a line-item breakout for CFO.
2) Marissa: please prepare SOW addendum language to co-term add-ons and include proration clause.
3) Ben: send finalized blended rate calc and redlined sample with the exec concession noted.

If you want a quick call to finalize, I'm available tomorrow 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
